history.title: History & Roots
history.subtitle: The story of Dhanana begins with a man named Dhanna Jaat

origin.heading: The Origin Story
origin.text: The name Dhanana traces back to its founder, Dhanna Jaat, who established this settlement centuries ago. What began as a single homestead grew into a thriving agricultural community rooted in the fertile plains of Haryana.
origin.clan: The Ghanghas Jat clan has been the dominant community since the village's founding — their lineage and legacy woven into every corner of Dhanana.

timeline.foundingDesc: A single settler stakes his claim on the Haryana plains, naming his home after himself.
timeline.ghanghasDesc: The Ghanghas become the dominant clan, shaping the village's identity and social structure.
timeline.agricultureDesc: Rice fields cover half the land. Millet and cotton fill the rest. Dhanana feeds the region.
timeline.expansionDesc: Dhanana I, II, and III form as farmers begin living in distant fields — Jatai, Sukhpura, and Kuchpad are born.
timeline.modernDesc: Schools, hospitals, markets, and paved roads connect Dhanana to the wider world.

neighbors.heading: Neighboring Villages
neighbors.desc: Dhanana sits at the heart of a cluster of villages, bound by shared history and geography.

demographics.title: Demographics
demographics.subtitle: A portrait of Dhanana's people — from Census 2011
demographics.sexRatioContext: Haryana state average is 879. This honest statistic reflects a challenge shared across the region — one that Dhanana and Haryana are working to address.

culture.title: Culture & Heritage
culture.subtitle: The living soul of Dhanana — language, sport, faith, and harvest

languages.heading: Languages
languages.desc: The people of Dhanana speak Hindi and the proud Haryanvi dialect — a language of warmth, wit, and deep-rooted identity.

sport.heading: Handball Capital
sport.desc: Dhanana has produced national-level handball players. Sport is not just recreation here — it is pride, discipline, and community.

crops.heading: The Fields of Dhanana
crops.desc: Rice covers half the cultivated land. Millet and cotton fill the rest. The agricultural calendar defines the rhythm of life.

temples.heading: Sacred Temples
temples.desc: Nine temples stand in Dhanana, drawing devotees from neighboring villages and as far as Nepal.
temples.devotees: Draws devotees from across the region, including Nepal
